V1.titulo: CASE V1: Complete valid input with network name
V1.salida: Expected output: valid case. Expected codes: none. It should correctly recognize the instruction, pass lexical, syntactic and semantic analysis, and generate three VLSM subnets for Office.

V2.titulo: CASE V2: Valid input without a network name
V2.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-007. It should generate the VLSM table using the base IP to identify the network and warn that NAME was not specified.

V3.titulo: CASE V3: Valid input with a single host quantity
V3.salida: Expected output: valid case. Expected codes: none. It should pass all three analysis phases and generate a single VLSM subnet for Laboratory.

V4.titulo: CASE V4: Valid input with multiple instructions
V4.salida: Expected output: valid case. Expected codes: none. It should recognize two valid blocks and generate the corresponding VLSM subnets for Administration and Systems.

V5.titulo: CASE V5: Valid input with hosts outside the recommended order
V5.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-008. It should accept the input, warn that HOSTS are not written from largest to smallest, and internally order them as 50,30,10 for the VLSM calculation.

V6.titulo: CASE V6: Valid input with reserved words attached to values
V6.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-002. It should recognize the input, generate the VLSM table, and warn that reserved words are attached directly to the following value.

V7.titulo: CASE V7: Valid input with a repeated network name
V7.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-003. Both instructions should be processed, but it should warn that the name Office was used for more than one network.

V8.titulo: CASE V8: Valid input with repeated host quantities
V8.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-004. It should generate three VLSM subnets and warn that the quantity 50 is repeated in the HOSTS list.

V9.titulo: CASE V9: Valid input with an oversized base network
V9.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-005. It should generate the requested subnet and warn that the base network has much more capacity than is actually required.

V10.titulo: CASE V10: Valid input with a generic network name
V10.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-006. It should generate the VLSM table and recommend using a more descriptive network name than Network.

V11.titulo: CASE V11: Valid input without an explicit name
V11.salida: Expected output: valid case with warning. Expected code: ADV-007. It should generate two subnets and recommend adding NAME followed by an identifier.

V12.titulo: CASE V12: Valid input with several different warnings
V12.salida: Expected output: valid case with several warnings. Expected codes: ADV-004, ADV-005, ADV-006, ADV-007. It should process both blocks and warn about repeated hosts, an oversized network, a generic name, and a missing network name.

V13.titulo: CASE V13: Valid input with missing name and hosts out of order
V13.salida: Expected output: valid case with several warnings. Expected codes: ADV-007, ADV-008. It should generate the subnets, recommend adding a network name, and warn that HOSTS should be written from largest to smallest.

V14.titulo: CASE V14: Valid input close to but below the oversizing threshold
V14.salida: Expected output: valid case. Expected codes: none. It should generate one VLSM subnet and not produce ADV-005 because the base network does not reach the threshold defined as clearly oversized.

I1.titulo: CASE I1: Lexical error caused by a misspelled reserved word
I1.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected codes: LEX-001, SIN-002. It should generate LEX-001 because MAS appears as an out-of-place identifier and SIN-002 because the reserved word MASK was not recognized after the IP address.

I2.titulo: CASE I2: Lexical error caused by an unrecognized symbol
I2.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: LEX-002. It should detect the @ symbol as an element that does not belong to the defined language.

I3.titulo: CASE I3: Lexical error caused by an out-of-place identifier
I3.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: LEX-001. It should generate a lexical error because Office appears as an identifier without being preceded by NAME.

I4.titulo: CASE I4: Syntax error caused by an incomplete IP address
I4.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-001. It should generate a syntax error because a complete IPv4 address was expected after IP.

I5.titulo: CASE I5: Syntax error caused by missing MASK
I5.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-002. It should generate a syntax error because the reserved word MASK was expected after the IP address.

I6.titulo: CASE I6: Syntax error caused by a mask without a slash
I6.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-003. It should generate a syntax error because a CIDR mask with a slash, for example /24, was expected after MASK.

I7.titulo: CASE I7: Syntax error caused by a missing host quantity
I7.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-004. It should generate a syntax error because at least one numeric quantity was expected after HOSTS.

I8.titulo: CASE I8: Syntax error caused by a double comma in the host list
I8.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-005. It should generate a syntax error because another NUMBER was expected after a comma.

I9.titulo: CASE I9: Syntax error caused by a trailing comma without another host
I9.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-005. It should generate a syntax error because the HOSTS list ends with a comma and no following quantity.

I10.titulo: CASE I10: Syntax error caused by NAME without an identifier
I10.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-006. It should generate a syntax error because an identifier was expected after NAME.

I11.titulo: CASE I11: Syntax error caused by NAME before another instruction begins
I11.salida: Expected output: invalid case with partial processing. Expected codes: SIN-006, ADV-001. It should reject the first instruction because NAME is incomplete and keep the second valid block so processing can continue.

I12.titulo: CASE I12: Syntax error caused by an exact duplicate instruction
I12.salida: Expected output: invalid case with partial processing. Expected codes: SIN-007, ADV-001. It should keep only one valid copy, report the duplicated instruction, and warn that processing will continue only with accepted blocks.

I13.titulo: CASE I13: Syntax error because HOSTS appears where MASK was expected
I13.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SIN-002. It should generate a syntax error because MASK was expected after the IP address but HOSTS appeared instead.

I14.titulo: CASE I14: Semantic error caused by a mask outside the allowed range
I14.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SEM-001. It should generate a semantic error because mask /31 is outside the allowed /8 to /30 range.

I15.titulo: CASE I15: Semantic error because the IP is not a network address
I15.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SEM-002. It should generate a semantic error because 192.168.1.5 is a host address for /24 and the corresponding network address is 192.168.1.0.

I16.titulo: CASE I16: Semantic error caused by a host quantity equal to zero
I16.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SEM-003. It should generate a semantic error because every quantity requested in HOSTS must be greater than zero.

I17.titulo: CASE I17: Semantic error caused by an individual request that is too large
I17.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected codes: SEM-004, SEM-005. It should generate SEM-005 because a request for 50 hosts needs a block larger than the entire /30 network, and SEM-004 because the total required capacity also exceeds what is available.

I18.titulo: CASE I18: Semantic error because the total number of subnets does not fit
I18.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected code: SEM-004. Each request can individually form a subnet, but together the three VLSM blocks require more addresses than are available in a /24 network.

I19.titulo: CASE I19: Semantic error caused by overlapping base networks
I19.salida: Expected output: invalid case with partial processing. Expected code: SEM-006. The second network should be rejected because its range lies within the first base network, while the first may remain as a semantically valid block.

I20.titulo: CASE I20: Mixed lexical, syntactic and semantic errors
I20.salida: Expected output: invalid case with several diagnostics. Expected codes: LEX-001, LEX-002, SIN-002, SEM-001, SEM-003. It should produce diagnostics from all three phases. The first instruction contains semantic problems and an unknown symbol, while the second contains an invalid word instead of MASK and a malformed host list.

I21.titulo: CASE I21: Lexical error caused by incorrect capitalization of a reserved word
I21.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected codes: LEX-003, SIN-002. It should generate LEX-003 because mask must be written exactly as MASK and then SIN-002 because the parser does not receive a valid MASK reserved word.

I22.titulo: CASE I22: Lexical error caused by a number directly joined to text
I22.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected codes: LEX-004, SIN-004. It should generate LEX-004 because 50ABC mixes a numeric value with text without separation, and SIN-004 because the syntactic phase ends without receiving a valid HOSTS quantity.

I23.titulo: CASE I23: Lexical error caused by a CIDR mask directly joined to text
I23.salida: Expected output: invalid case. Expected codes: LEX-004, SIN-003. It should generate LEX-004 because /24HOSTS joins a numeric mask with text, and SIN-003 because the parser does not receive a valid CIDR mask after MASK.

I24.titulo: CASE I24: Syntax error caused by starting with out-of-order tokens and later recovery
I24.salida: Expected output: invalid case with partial processing. Expected codes: SIN-008, ADV-001. It should generate SIN-008 because the first line starts outside the expected structure, recover at the next instruction, and correctly process the network Second.

I25.titulo: CASE I25: Errors from all three phases with recovery of a valid block
I25.salida: Expected output: invalid case with partial processing and several diagnostics. Expected codes: LEX-001, LEX-002, SIN-002, SEM-001, SEM-003, ADV-001. It should demonstrate that TecNet Finder can report lexical, syntactic and semantic errors and still recover the third valid instruction so its VLSM calculation can continue.
